title: Refactor: Change flowDB to class based architecture.
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

- Refactors the existing flowDb implementation from a functional approach to a class-based architecture to improve code organization, maintainability, and extensibility.
- Return a new DB object when `diagramObject.db` is called.
- Introduces new FlowDB class to encapsulate database operations and state
- Migrates existing functions to class methods
- Maintains existing API interface for backwards compatibility
- Following functions still uses common DB:
  - defaultConfig
  - setAccTitle
  - setAccDescription
  - setDiagramTitle
  - getAccTitle
  - getAccDescription
  - getDiagramTitle
- Reason why above functions still uses common DB: https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/pull/6161#discussion_r1913261481

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

- The flowDb module previously relied on functions and global variables. Consequently, each call to mermaid.parse or mermaid.render resulted in changes to global variables.
- This behavior caused issues when rendering multiple diagrams using the same Mermaid API, as the database object (DB) for the diagrams would get mixed up.
- To address this, flowDb was refactored into a class-based structure. This change ensures that each diagramObject.db call creates a new instance of the database (DB), preventing conflicts between diagrams.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
Hey @saurabhg772244, can you update your PR description on why we're using public class instance fields with arrow functions instead of class methods? (please also remove "class methods" from your PR description, unless you are planning on using them!).

E.g. that since https://github.com/zaach/jison/commit/157cdd6bf23920c6282f06534b3f12204b31e90a and https://github.com/zaach/jison/blob/cbf9d933677fb14b8526ee146586348139e2fb73/lib/jison.js#L1390-L1395, JISON instead makes a copy of the passed object, but only copies direct properties, not class methods which are part of object's `prototype`.

So all functions used in the `flowchart.jison` file can't be class methods.

For the other functions (e.g. private functions), please also add your reasoning (but it could just be as simple as consistency with the other public values that have to be instance fields).

---

Can you also add proof that class instance fields won't break Mermaid on older browsers? Looking at https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Classes/Public_class_fields, it sounds like there's a chance that this could break Mermaid on Safari 15.6 and earlier, so I think we need to be sure that this isn't a breaking change, otherwise we might need to rethink how this PR is implemented.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags a potentially blocking issue with using arrow function class fields and suggests switching to regular method syntax.
